text: When developers work with APIs, they use HTTP requests to send and receive data between applications. Most modern APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy for both humans and machines to read. Before making requests, you often need authentication—usually an API key—to prove you have permission to access the service. However, don’t forget about rate limits; APIs typically allow only a certain number of requests per minute, so plan your calls carefully. Finally, always include error handling in your code—like checking for 404 or 500 responses—so you can manage failures gracefully and debug issues quickly.
